svg.title: Engineering simulation software landscape
svg.desc: A role map comparing BAB-CS numerical governance with device-oriented SPICE tools, PLECS power-electronics systems, Simscape Electrical multiple-physics systems, and Xyce large-scale parallel simulation.
svg.text: Simulation software roles across an engineering program
The tools overlap, but their official emphasis and best handoff point differ. This is a workflow map, not a ranking.
BAB-CS · NUMERICAL GOVERNANCE AND REPRODUCIBILITY
Supervise candidate methods and preserve the evidence behind accepted transients
Best fit: bounded method studies, failure-cause analysis, reduced-order switched experiments, qualification, and teaching.
NGSPICE + LTSPICE · DEVICE-ORIENTED CIRCUIT DESIGN
Device-oriented analog and mixed-signal workflows
Best handoff: detailed models, vendor macromodels,
schematic capture, waveform inspection, and mapped checks.
PLECS · POWER-ELECTRONICS SYSTEM DESIGN
Converters, controls, switching, thermal, and deployment
Best handoff: converter design, control verification,
thermal studies, code generation, and real-time controller tests.
SIMSCAPE ELECTRICAL · MULTIPLE-PHYSICS SYSTEMS
Electrical, mechanical, thermal, motors, grids, and controls
Best handoff: system integration, virtual testing, fault studies,
cross-domain control design, code generation, and hardware tests.
XYCE · LARGE-SCALE PARALLEL CIRCUIT SIMULATION
SPICE-compatible simulation for extremely large problems
Best handoff: high-performance analog networks,
very large circuit studies, and serial or parallel execution.
Recommended engineering pattern
Use BAB-CS to qualify the reduced numerical experiment and its authority chain; move to the specialist simulator when the project requires
broader device fidelity, vendor models, multiple-physics plants, hardware-in-the-loop deployment, or very-large-scale parallel execution.
